summary: Owner betting case study — UFC 333, Petr Yan vs Merab Dvalishvili (Oct 24, 2026, Abu Dhabi). START: the market (Kalshi priced Merab the favorite, ~57c), the statistics pages, and ForgeClaw's own framework all leaned Dvalishvili; ForgeClaw's seven-section research run returned no framework bet (its conditional Merab trigger never filled). Merab took the first fight on wrestling and pace; Yan adjusted in the second and had his number from there. EXPLICITLY NOT THE BASIS: Merab's weight cut (that came from the app's simulation report, not the owner). END GAME: Yan won the decision and retained the UFC bantamweight title; the position (42 Yan YES contracts at ~59.6c average, $25 staked natively in the Kalshi app) settles $41.87 (+$16.87); the $25-to-$100 plan stands ~42% complete. The chamber learns this record WITH its documented basis attached, so what it learns is the grounded kind of conviction.

summary: Owner fight-analysis principle, generalized from the Yan-Merab trilogy case (ref UFC333-YAN-20261024) and formulated with ChatGPT (relayed by owner 2026-10-24): MATCHUP-BASED CAUSAL REASONING — analyze how fighters interact, not just how good each looks individually. Method: (1) identify each fighter's primary path to victory; (2) look for evidence of tactical adaptation across previous matchups; (3) test whether one fighter has demonstrated the ability to neutralize the other's key strength (Yan, fight 2: defended Merab's takedowns over five rounds after losing fight 1 to wrestling/pace); (4) reassess the matchup that REMAINS if that strength is neutralized (a standing fight, where Yan's Muay Thai held a substantial edge); (5) combine with current statistics, striking/grappling data, and explicit uncertainty — prior-matchup evidence supports a hypothesis, it never guarantees a repeat. Calibration rule: preserve the tactical thesis with each prediction and grade this reasoning TYPE against outcomes across many fights, so the pattern earns or loses weight on its track record; one win does not canonize it. Companion to the Yan case record, whose grounded owner read carries weight per the owner's 2026-10-24 override.
provenance: Owner's own summary in chat 2026-10-24 ~16:57 CDT ('I think that's really important to put that in the corpus and to look at fights that way'); principle formulation by ChatGPT, relayed and endorsed by the owner in chat 2026-10-24 ~16:58 CDT; underlying case + weight override on issue #235 (comment 6389547803) and PR #294.

summary: Owner GO (2026-10-24): MiroFish swarm-simulation lane starts, inside FUSION, weight ZERO until earned. MiroFish is an open-source AGPL-3.0 swarm engine (persona agents on a simulated social network, CAMEL-AI OASIS) - a crowd-convergence signal, sentiment family, not an outcome oracle. Independent evidence (OrcaLayer Polymarket test): swarm medians clustered 20-55, no clear signal - hence earn-your-weight. Weight policy: 0 until >=10 settled comparable sims AND >=55% directional hits (crowd lane bars), then capped 10% inside FUSION; the 5c approve bar reads FUSION without the sim until earned; sim never enters requote/shard/sizing math. Records: sim-run (seed-packet provenance, engine config, median lean, report link) + sim-outcome at settlement (hit/miss, distance), graded wins and losses, no cherry-picking. Server-side only, ~$0.40/run ceiling, one sim per market per card. AGPL: external process, never vendored into the proprietary repo.

H1 PRICE-CONVERGENCE: WRONG SHAPE. On 1,005,745 prints / 31 settled KXBTC15M windows, the favored side's price-to-outcome gap decays as a POWER LAW in remaining time (gap ~ 1.06 * r^0.556, R2 0.949) with linear close behind (0.947); the exponential finishes third (tau 685s, R2 0.907; median-gap fit tau 431s). Forced exponential half-life 300-475s is not a system constant: the empirical half-life collapses ~575s (early) -> ~230s (late) -> ~25s (final minute, gap 18.5c at r~55 to ~1-3c at r~25). As a mispricing claim it is unmeasurable: excess over the calibration-implied gap 2p(1-p) sits within -4.5..+1.6c of zero in every 30s bucket — what decays is unresolved uncertainty, not a mispricing reservoir. Tape leg also non-exponential (linear R2 0.78 > exp 0.63): tape wrong-side probability 46.7% at open -> 5.3% at close. Full fits: briefs/exponential-time-study-2026-10-28.md.

H2 ACTIVITY RAMP: WRONG SHAPE globally, exponential only in the endgame. Contract volume per minute is flat (~3-5.5% share) for minutes 0-9, then: last 5 min 54.4% of all contracts, last 3 min 40.5%, last 1 min 17.5%. Full-window exp fit on contracts: doubling 7.5 min, R2(log) 0.74; power law in remaining time fits better (contracts ~ r^-0.58, R2 0.90); the final-5-minutes segment is a true local exponential (doubling 2.7 min, R2 0.994). The ramp is SIZE not count: prints only 2.2x first-to-last minute while contracts/print grow ~69 -> ~191. Public check stated precisely: DegenHedge's 89% is the share of last-3-min contracts at <=10c/>=90c prices — our universe corroborates at 84.6%; our last-3 share of ALL contracts (40.5%) is a different statistic.

H3 SETTLEMENT-INFLUENCE DECAY: the curve is EXACT ARITHMETIC and LINEAR, not exponential. Settlement = mean of the 60 one-second BRTI prints of the final minute, so a sustained spot move S starting with R seconds left shifts the average by at most S * min(1, R/60): influence fraction 1.0 for R>=60, 0.75 at R=45, 0.50 at R=30, 0.167 at R=10 (transient form: S * overlap-seconds/60). Empirical verification UNMEASURABLE at the Bank's tape cadence: tape-distance->print-price betas over ~12s intervals in the final 180s are noise (corr -0.12..+0.10, unstable signs), and the tape's last sample lands at elapsed 845-860s — the Bank is blind for the final ~40-55s of every window, exactly where the influence fraction collapses.

C1 THE CLOCK (derived): the exponential does NOT explain the opportunity-lifetime zeros. Crossings precede confirmations: the favored side's first >=85c print lands at median elapsed 444s (31/31 windows), first >=90c at 499s, vs gate passes at median ~617s — by confirmation the residual gap (~3c at a 97c print) is ~the taker fee, so the capture window at confirmation is zero by sequencing, not by decay during our reaction. The one real sub-85 lifetime (10.7s) is 0.02-0.04 of any fitted half-life; at crossings the ask repriced ~0.4c/s (80->82c in 5.1s). Hardware graded: 12s tape cadence is fine vs the slow regime but the tape ENDS ~45s before expiry (blind through the influence collapse); the ~5s order chain lost its only race at the crossing, ~3 min before the chain starts. A capture window exists only pre-confirmation, where the gap is uncertainty (46.7% tape wrong-rate at open), not edge.

C2 COMPOUNDING (derived): at the 5% stake cap each trade multiplies bankroll by (1 + 0.05*e/p); goal $18.76->$40 = x2.132. At the shadow grid's MEASURED expectancy (26 graded, modeled net -263c, e = -10.12c/contract aggregate) the bankroll HALVES every ~116 trades (~26 days at the observed ~4.5 graded/day/variant pace) and expected time-to-goal is never — negative drift. Per variant halving: band-090 ~62 trades, dist-090 ~79, dist090-band085 ~103, dist-080 ~236, band-085 ~1380. At hypothetical edges (p=85c): +2c/contract -> goal in ~644 trades (~143d at 4.5/day, ~32d at 20/day); +5c -> ~258 trades (~57d / ~13d). Even a proven +5c edge — larger than anything found in this market all week — cannot compound to the goal inside a day-scale mandate: the goal is a season, not a session. Exponential time is the goal's friend only above zero edge and its enemy below.
